files.purpose: Holds Droppy Code's per-Mac preference model: the @MainActor @Observable final class AppSettings. It owns every user-defaults key (private enum Key, :117-180), and each stored property writes itself back in its own didSet with no save step. init() (:707-790) reads every key with its shipped default from `CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard`. It also defines the settings-facing enums TextGenerationChoice, ThreadFinishAction, SidebarMode and ActivityThreadStyle with their user-visible titles and detail strings, and the ModelPin and ModelPreference value types. It is the single owner of the four provider API keys (DeepSeek, Meta, Z.ai, Command Code). They are read from the Keychain lazily and once, off the main thread through Task.detached, with an isReadingKeychain guard so the fill never writes back. Edits go to the Keychain, and a plaintext defaults copy is kept only when the Keychain refuses the key. In B3 the key code goes straight through APIKeychain by ProviderKind, via the new helpers storedKey(for:fallback:) and storeAPIKeyChange(_:from:provider:fallbackKey:), instead of the four per-provider *Keychain wrappers. Finally, it serves as the ProviderSettings the provider registry reads (binary paths, enabled providers, last model and effort, API keys with login-environment fallback), and as the store for Hydra pairs, the composer's model list (15-entry cap) and per-model preferences.

feature_notes: B2 to B3 (churn 42: 10 hunks, +23/-19 lines, 947 to 951 lines): no user-visible or persisted behaviour of AppSettings changed. Every hunk is a refactor that follows two upstream reorganisations elsewhere.

Hunks 1, 9 and 10 (:184, :708, :869): `WebsiteCaptures.defaults ?? .standard` became `CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard`. At B2, WebsiteCaptures.defaults was only a nonisolated read-through to CaptureRun.defaults, and B3 deleted those read-through properties from App/Captures/WebsiteCaptures.swift, so the resolved suite is the same. The capture suite is still 'iordv.droppycode.website-captures' (CaptureRun.swift:40), and the branch is still the user-unreachable capture short circuit that porting/dead_code.md entry 44 lists; that entry still quotes the B2 text and line 183.

Hunks 2 to 5 (the four API-key didSets, now :367-400): each three-line body (guard, <Provider>Keychain.setAPIKey, storeAPIKeyFallback) became one call to the new private storeAPIKeyChange(_:from:provider:fallbackKey:) (:481-487). That helper holds the same guard `!isReadingKeychain, value != oldValue`, calls `APIKeychain.setKey(value, for: provider)` and then `storeAPIKeyFallback(kept ? "" : value, forKey: fallbackKey)`. The provider-to-fallback-key pairing is unchanged (.deepseek/deepseekAPIKey, .meta/metaAPIKey, .zai/zaiAPIKey, .commandcode/commandcodeAPIKey).

Hunks 6 and 7 (readKeys :434-441 plus the new storedKey(for:fallback:) :443-445): the reads now go through `APIKeychain.key(for: provider, fallback: "")` instead of DeepSeekKeychain/MetaKeychain/ZaiKeychain/CommandCodeKeychain.apiKey(fallback: ""). Those four Swift files were deleted in B3, and their account strings moved verbatim into APIKeychain.account(for:) (APIKeychain.swift:26-34), so the same four Keychain items are read and written.

The one real storage-semantics change is outside this file: APIKeychain.set at B3 tries SecItemUpdate first and adds only on errSecItemNotFound (APIKeychain.swift:50-57), where B2 did SecItemDelete then SecItemAdd. AppSettings only sees the Bool it returns and treats it as before. Records whose text says 'delete then add' (PR-PROVAPI-003, PR-PROVREG-088, PR-SETTINGS-272) must be reclassified by the APIKeychain.swift bundle.
